summary: Clearwater NF 10-foot L-4 lookout in Idaho County; built 1931 or 1932, abandoned after 1933, condemned and burned in 1946; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 10-foot round native timber tower with an L-4 lookout cabin
facts.status_note: Condemned and burned in 1946; no source describes what remains at the site

access.note: On Clearwater National Forest land; the Idaho Fire Lookouts site files it as a hike-in site

visit.trail_note: Hartig says trail #225 from Fish Creek was built in 1931 to reach the site

events.note: firelookout.com, the Idaho Fire Lookouts site and the 2016 Forest Service list give 1932; Hartig's 1981 history dates the trail and tower work to 1931
Abandoned after the 1933 season; lookouts set up that year on Boundary Peak and Frenchman Butte covered nearly the same view
Condemned and burned in a forest-wide cleanup of surplus buildings (Hartig); the Forest Lookouts summary gives duplicated seen areas as the reason

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Hartig's 1981 history dates the work to 1931, while firelookout.com, the Idaho Fire Lookouts site and the 2016 Forest Service list give 1932. The event records 1932 and its note keeps the 1931 date.

Hartig gives a forest-wide cleanup of surplus buildings; the Forest Lookouts summary gives duplicated seen areas. Both agree the tower was condemned and burned in 1946, so only the reason is recorded in two forms.

sources.title: Ant Hill (quoting Louis Hartig, Historic Facilities of the Lochsa Ranger District, 1981)
Clearwater National Forest Lookouts (list compiled by Margaret Sand, Walde Lookout and Cindy Schacher, June 2016)

notes_for_editor: Built year conflicts: Hartig (1931) against three sources (1932); recorded 1932 with the 1931 date in the note. No source describes what remains at the site today, so the story says so. Public access rests on national forest ownership and the hike-in label only; no current access rules were found. No staffing names are documented, so the story says nothing about staff.
